## Do I Really Need to Worry About Token Efficiency?

::: {.fragment}
- Maybe not now, but eventually. AI tokens will never again be as subsidized by the AI giants as they are today. And setups with data privacy are not subsidized.
:::
::: {.fragment}
- We live in the AI-token equivalent of a pre-1973 oil crisis - the era of cheap and abundant tokens. 
:::
::: {.fragment}
- Enjoy it will it last -- **it will never again be as cheap to experiment and learn with tokens as it is now**.
:::
::: {.fragment}
- Those who started to use WBG's GitHub Copilot licenses last spring or have recently gone from personal Claude licenses to use WB Claude Enterprise have already experienced some "_oil-crises_".
:::
::: {.fragment}
- We can afford to drive a V8 Cadillac Eldorado today, but need to learn how to drive a hybrid Toyota Prius tomorrow.
:::
::: {.fragment}
- The AI companies' gigantic company valuations depends on us getting too comfortable in our Cadillacs before they hike the prices.
:::

## Enterprise Tokens are NOT overly expensive

::: {.fragment}
* Running large language models (LLMs) is expensive: **_very_** expensive.
:::
::: {.fragment}
* Therefore, **enterprise credits _are not overpriced_**: they are priced to reflect the cost of running these models.
:::
::: {.fragment}
* Instead, **personal license credits _are artificially cheap_**: Anthropic, OpenAI, and others subsidize usage in exchange for access to your data and to compete for market share.
:::
::: {.fragment}
* With a higher-tier personal subscription, you can opt out of a greater amount of data collection -- but it requires that **you regularly review new privacy settings**, and **you can never opt out of all data collection** unless you sign an enterprise license agreement.
:::
::: {.fragment}
* **A $20 personal license will give you much more usage than a $20 enterprise license**: this is the premium we pay for privacy.
:::
